diagnosis: release_hijack_session accepts original_user_id from the user-controlled request body rather than restoring the previous session from a cryptographically signed server session variable. An attacker can call this release endpoint with an administrative user ID to bypass authentication and take over superuser accounts.

corrected_code:
from ninja import Router
from ninja.security import HttpBearer
from ninja.errors import HttpError
from django.contrib.auth import get_user_model, login
from hijack.helpers import release_hijack

User = get_user_model()
hijack_session_router = Router(auth=HttpBearer())

@hijack_session_router.post("/hijack/release")
def release_hijack_session(request):
    # Use django-hijack helper which validates server-stored hijack session stack
    if not request.session.get('is_hijacked_user', False):
        raise HttpError(400, "No active hijack session to release")

    release_hijack(request)
    return {"status": "released", "active_user": request.user.username}
